title: The Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Neural Complexity in Patients with Focal Cortical Dysplasia
summary: Focal cortical dysplasia is a common cause of epilepsy in children and young adults, and medication often does not provide sufficient relief. The condition can lead to recurrent seizures and impair thinking, learning, or behavior. Cases in which changes in the brain are not visible on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are particularly challenging, as this makes it difficult to plan surgery. Recent studies show that brain activity and connectivity change in epilepsy and that signals in affected brain regions often become less diverse and flexible. Such changes could help identify abnormal brain regions more effectively and improve treatment for patients.

interventions.name:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-    Adult patients with MRI-positive findings and suspected FCD Type IIB.
-    Adult patients with unilateral focal epilepsy for whom the location of the seizure focus and the irritative zone was determined during video-EEG monitoring according to Rosenow & Lüders (2001).
-    Adult patients with psychogenic non-epileptic seizures without epilepsy, who will serve as the control group.
-    Voluntary participation following an explanation of the benefits and risks of the study.
-    Verbal and written consent from the participant to participate in the study and to have data collected.
Exclusion criteria:
-    Common exclusion criteria for undergoing an fMRI scan, such as
o    Pacemaker
o    Vagus nerve stimulator
o    Neurostimulator or drug infusion pump
o	Metal objects near the head (e.g., splinters, surgical clips or staples, cochlear implants; also: metal splinters in the body, e.g., due to work in the metalworking industry)
o    Recent skull fractures
o    Alcohol consumption within the last 12 hours prior to the examination
-    Alcoholism, medication abuse, and drug abuse
-    Confirmed or suspected pregnancy based on medical history 
-    Participants who lack legal capacity
